description: Behavioral mutations for public geometry, model, migration, filament validation, tool ordering, wipe-tower and G-code contracts. Mutation results are recorded separately from this inventory.

mutants.description: The non-vertex length split must append the analytically interpolated 3D point to both pieces; the test checks the shared endpoint, both lengths, and source immutability.
Appended source fitting records must start at the destination/source shared vertex index; the test requires the source linear record to be rebased from 0..2 to 1..3.
Reversing a fitted path must reverse metadata record order after rebasing indices; the test checks the reversed record range and a second reversal restores the original metadata.
Clipping must remove the requested terminal 3D distance, including the Z component; the test checks the analytic endpoint and measured length delta.
The public tolerance lookup must reject an exact-distance boundary; the candidate checks strict-boundary behavior.
Adjacent equal points are the only points removed by the public duplicate cleanup contract.
first_intersection must select the hit nearest to line.a; the diagonal crosses both U arms and the reversed query checks the opposite nearest hit.

Row 1 looks ahead to 0 -> 1, where only the new tool 1 is soluble; dropping the new-tool disjunct makes row 1 match the all-insoluble control and fail its finite grid geometry/material inequalities.
Row 2 looks ahead to 1 -> 0, where only the old tool 1 is soluble; dropping the old-tool disjunct makes row 2 match the all-insoluble control and fail its finite grid geometry/material inequalities.

Suppress the backward skip-range adjustment for a reachable heating insertion. The corrected fixture selects the in-skip move before adjust_iter; without relocation the public M104/M632/M633 insertion falls inside SKIPPABLE_START/END.
Drop the public M633 close marker while preserving the skippable branch and its variable use. The corrected fixture requires the complete M632/M104/M633 transition before the source skip interval.

The dedicated-filament row requires the configured third filament on active wipe-tower layers while the ordinary row remains free of it; inverting the partition gate removes the required active-layer witness and cannot be hidden by model material output.

The safe disabled-insertion mutant preserves the zero-filament control guard but rejects every configured positive ID; the dedicated row then lacks filament 2 on active tower layers while no invalid index is ever constructed.

With the same two-material geometry, enabling prime-tower soluble preference changes the explicit first-layer order from filament 0 first to filament 1 first; disabling this gate leaves the soluble row indistinguishable from the ordinary control.
The soluble first-layer row explicitly requires filament 1 before filament 0; suppressing the source swap preserves both tools but fails that independent order oracle.

Route an explicitly selected support filament back to the object's extruder. The support-filament=2 case must then lose the incompatible second material and fail its exact blocking/warning oracle, while the support-filament=1 control remains compatible.

Require both recommended range bounds to be missing before material defaults are resolved. The PLA row with an explicit low bound and missing high bound must remain a valid HighLowMixed result; the mutant returns InvalidTemperatureRange.
